findings.title: Light-theme lightness changed from 30% to 70% for embedded post author links
findings.body: The original was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The new light branch is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), with the dark branch at $secondary 30%. The PR only intends to add a dark-theme variant, so the light-theme colour should stay at 30%. Using 70% makes these links much lighter and lowers contrast on light themes. The same mistake appears to have been copied from the .username.new-user rule.

findings.title: Light-theme colour of .group-member-info .name silently changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%). The new light branch is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), and the dark branch is $secondary 50%. This alters the existing light-theme appearance, making the name lighter and identical to .title. The other name rules in this file use 30%/70%, so the correct pair would be 30% for $primary and 70% for $secondary. The same regression is in mobile/user.scss.

findings.title: Light-theme colour of .custom-message-length changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%). The new light branch is scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), with the dark branch at $secondary 70%. The pairs are swapped relative to the desktop modal.scss, which correctly uses 70%/30%. As a result the mobile light theme gets a much darker hint text and the dark theme gets a lighter one, instead of a pure dark-theme fix.

findings.title: Topic-map h3 light colour changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original rule was scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%). The new rule uses 50%/50% for the light/dark branches. This lightens the existing light-theme heading and makes it match h4. The desktop version correctly uses 20%/80%, and so does the .number rule on mobile. The correct pair would be 20% and 80%.
